messages:
Maria (CS): Heads-up — ACME called in. New hires are syncing via SCIM but aren't getting the 'developer' role assigned. Also reported that when employees leave the org they still have console access. Escalating; customer is worried about data access.

Emily - ACME Admin: Repro steps from our side: 1) Invite new user in Okta > push group membership to Redwood via SCIM. 2) User appears in Redwood users list but role column is blank. 3) When we deactivate user in Okta, user still can log in to Redwood Console.

Alex (Support): Thanks Emily. Can you paste the SCIM logs (redwood side) or any HTTP responses you see? Also confirm which SCIM integration token you're using (service token name) and whether any recent changes were made to group names or role mappings in the Console.

Emily - ACME Admin: Here's the SCIM request we see in Okta (pushed group membership):

```
PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/abc123
Authorization: Bearer scim_XXXXX
Content-Type: application/json

{ "operations": [ { "op": "add", "path": "members", "value": [{ "value": "u-789", "display": "sarah@example.com" }] } ] }
```

Okta reports 200 OK. On the Redwood side the audit shows a 200 for the group update but the user role mapping log says "no matching role mapping for group 'Engineering - EMEA'".

Alex (Support): Hmm. Can you also paste the mapping config screenshot or JSON from Console > Provisioning > Group Mappings?

Emily - ACME Admin: Screenshot attached in ticket but here's the exported mapping config they gave us: 

```
{
  "mappings": [
    { "group_name": "Engineers", "role": "developer" },
    { "group_name": "Admins", "role": "admin" }
  ]
}
```

Note: Our Okta group is named "Engineering - EMEA" (not "Engineers") because of region suffixing via lifecycle rules. Not sure if Console supports wildcard/group substring mapping.

Sam (Identity): This is already looking like a mismatch between Okta group displayName and the mapping key. Redwood's SCIM processor matches on group.displayName by default. If Okta pushes a different displayName (or you use group externalId) the mapping won't match. Also worth checking token scopes — if the SCIM token doesn't have groups:write or users:patch scopes we could see partial behavior.

Emily - ACME Admin: Our SCIM token is the one labeled "acme-scim-integration" created 6 months ago. No one rotated it recently. What exact scopes does Redwood need? Okta doesn't surfacing scopes clearly in the integration UI.

Jordan (Eng): From the runtime side — the processor supports two matching modes configured in Console: "displayName_exact" and "externalId". Default is displayName_exact. If your provisioning pipeline adds suffixes we either need a mapping for each variant or enable externalId matching (requires Okta to push group.externalId with stable id). The deprovision behavior: when Okta deactivates a user we expect a PATCH to /scim/v2/Users/:id with active=false. If Okta is sending a delete or setting `active:false` but not removing group membership, the Console should still remove roles because role assignment is derived from present group membership. Do you have examples of the user deactivate payload?

Emily - ACME Admin: Okta sends a PUT to /scim/v2/Users/u-789 with active=false. In our audit we see the incoming PUT and Redwood replies 204. Yet the user still retains the role in UI and can access. Log snippet from our audit (redacted):

```
2024-06-25T14:12:03Z INFO scim:received PUT /scim/v2/Users/u-789
2024-06-25T14:12:03Z DEBUG scim:applied attribute update {"active":false}
2024-06-25T14:12:03Z INFO roles:recompute user_id=u-789 result=no-op (no role change found)
```

That "no-op" seems wrong — we expected a recompute that removed the 'developer' role.

Alex (Support): That log is useful. Sam / Jordan, could be a bug: recompute path not triggered for deactivation-only events when group membership history still indicates role. Maybe there's a TTL or cache; also check if the system ties roles to a separate membership table that isn't being updated by the user active flag.

Sam (Identity): I'm going to check the SCIM processor logic. Hypothesis A: Group mapping mismatch (displayName mismatch) causes assignments to be recorded in a derived table when applied via an explicit Group PATCH, but when Okta deactivates user via User PUT without removing group membership, the recompute code looks at live group membership (which remained because group push was never matched) so it thinks user wasn't assigned by mapping and skips removal -> result: user keeps role. Hypothesis B: Token scopes insufficient earlier allowed group pushes but didn't allow users:patch events to be processed fully. Need to confirm token audit entries.

Jordan (Eng): Repro plan: 1) Create a dummy Okta group named exactly "Engineers" and push a member to Redwood via SCIM PATCH to Groups. 2) Observe assignment in Console and in roles audit table. 3) Deactivate user via PUT active:false. 4) Verify recompute path clears role. If it clears in this controlled test then mapping mismatch is likely root cause. If not, there may be a codepath bug.

Alex (Support): Emily — can you perform the controlled test in your sandbox Okta and paste results? If you can't, we can run a test from our staging SCIM client and share steps.

Emily - ACME Admin: I can run a quick test later today. Before that, how can I confirm which group attribute Redwood is matching on? Console UI isn't explicit.

Sam (Identity): In the Console advisory we log mapping mode in Provisioning > Group Mappings. But to avoid UI friction you can call the SCIM Metadata endpoint we expose: GET /scim/v2/metadata returns a JSON blob with matchingMode. Example (from staging):

```
GET /scim/v2/metadata
Authorization: Bearer scim_XXXXX

Response: { "matchingMode": "displayName_exact", "supportedAttributes": ["displayName", "externalId"] }
```

If your matchingMode is displayName_exact you'll need exact displayName matches. If externalId available you can change Okta mapping to set group.externalId to a stable tag used in our mapping config.

Jordan (Eng): Also adding a quick check for token scopes: we record token scopes on every incoming request in the headers audit table. If you provide one raw request header (redact token) we can confirm scopes. Example header we look for: Authorization: Bearer scim_XXXXX (we map token id -> scopes internally).

Alex (Support): Short-term mitigation: create group aliases in Okta matching the names used in Redwood mapping (e.g., duplicate group named exactly "Engineers" and sync). Longer-term: switch to externalId matching or have us support prefix/wildcard mapping (we can evaluate).

Emily (ACME Admin): Ok I will try the alias approach and run the controlled test. ETA 2 hours. If that doesn't work I'll provide a sample request/response dump.

deploy-bot: Deployment 2024-06-25T15:00:00Z finished on infra/staging (commit abcdef) :white_check_mark:

Jordan (Eng): Noted. Alex and I will standby. If Emily's alias test fails we'll run the controlled test from staging tomorrow morning and forward results. Also creating a ticket for product to consider wildcard mapping options.

Alex (Support): Summary of next steps: 1) Emily tries alias group named exactly per mapping (short-term) 2) Emily runs controlled test and posts payloads/logs (today) 3) Sam/Jordan will validate token scopes in our audit logs and run staging repro if needed 4) Product will triage mapping UX improvement. We'll follow up in this thread.

Emily - ACME Admin: Thanks team 🙏 — I'll update once tests complete.

Maria (CS): Adding to account war room. Tagging Sam and Jordan for priority. @Sam @Jordan please advise if we should pause any auto-provision flows for ACME until resolved.

Sam (Identity): Please don't pause any production flows yet — the alias mitigation should be safe. I'll check audit logs for token scopes now and report back.
